Across all 23 assertions, 17 pass in both configurations and therefore do not discriminate in this single-run sample: coupling-lifecycle assertions 2-7, manager-architecture assertions 2-6, and networked-squad-ai assertions 1-6.

The 17 shared passes cover the bounded health-event design and lifecycle cleanup; GameManager decomposition, ScriptableObject/runtime-state separation, incremental migration, plain-C#/asmdef seams, and proportional DI/ECS decisions; and the squad-AI pipeline, technique selection, server authority, observability, determinism, and budget scheduling.

Six assertions uniquely separate the skill: coupling-lifecycle #1; manager-architecture #1, #7, and #8; and networked-squad-ai #7 and #8. Every one passes with the skill and fails without it; no assertion shows the reverse pattern.

Evidence classification is the only separator recurring in more than one eval: the no-skill coupling and manager outputs fail to separate supplied facts from uninspected repository/runtime facts, while the with-skill outputs label them explicitly. The no-skill AI verification assertion also lacks an explicit proposed-versus-executed distinction.

Complex lifecycle acceptance is another cross-eval separator: the no-skill manager output omits observable destination readiness and a return-to-menu/new-session flow, while the no-skill AI output leaves cancellation/despawn/pooled-reuse teardown and a PlayMode layer incomplete; the corresponding with-skill outputs pass.

Performance treatment is mostly shared rather than globally discriminating: both configurations pass the coupling and AI performance assertions; only manager-architecture separates, where the no-skill output lacks a representative player-build capture and reproducible before/after baseline.

In this sample, no-skill pass counts are 6/7 for coupling-lifecycle, 5/8 for manager-architecture, and 6/8 for networked-squad-ai; with-skill is 7/7, 8/8, and 8/8. The largest absolute separation is manager-architecture (+3 assertions), followed by AI (+2) and coupling (+1).

With-skill outputs are longer in every eval: 13,408 vs 9,374 chars (+4,034) for coupling, 22,376 vs 12,618 (+9,758) for manager, and 23,067 vs 15,575 (+7,492) for AI. The mean delta is +7,095 chars (+56.7%), alongside +1, +3, and +2 passed assertions respectively; this association does not establish causal efficiency.

Each eval has only one run per configuration, so these results do not support claims about variance, consistency, or flakiness; the aggregate standard deviation is across different eval prompts, not repeat executions.
Timing and token metrics were unavailable from the host. Their zero placeholders are not measurements, so this benchmark cannot support speed or token-cost comparisons.
